enAudit: G2-311 "Two Sentences: Full Stop or Question Mark?" — the instruction "Two sentences ran together, and one of them is a question" is FALSE on the page. The spec sets needQ:1, which guarantees one question per PAGE, not per lane; in the sweep render lane 3 ("the fig is next to the box max draws two figs for leo") contains no question at all. Either raise needQ to the lane count or make the claim page-level.

G1-304 "Write the Word: Every Clue" — the instruction "The word bank, the letter boxes and the first letter are all there to help." has NO imperative; it never tells the child to do anything. Every other face in write-the-word opens with a verb.

G1-296 / G1-297 — the picture rows OVERFLOW the white picture box at the top of the range. In g1296 cards 1, 4 and 5 and in g1297 card 3 the leftmost and rightmost icons are clipped by the card edge, so on a doubles/halves-WITH-PICTURES page the child is asked to count icons that are cut in half. Ten icons per row does not fit at that icon size.

G1-298 / G1-299 — the instruction says "No pictures to count", yet every card carries a 2x10 array of faint dots a child can literally count. The same panel is LABELLED "Draw it with blocks" on G1-256/G1-257, so it is a drawing area; here it is unlabelled and the copy denies it exists. Label it, or drop the "no pictures" claim.

G1-287 / G1-296 / G1-297 — three doubles-halves instructions are bare noun phrases with no imperative ("Every card on this page doubles a group of pictures.", "Bigger groups to double, all the way to twenty.", "Bigger groups of pictures to halve, all the way up to twenty."). They describe the page instead of telling a six-year-old what to write.

G1-301 "Word Bank and Letter Boxes" — every card carries three ruled writing lines AND a row of letter boxes, but the instruction names only the boxes ("Write one letter in each box"). The larger, more prominent control on the card goes unmentioned.

G1-282 "Unscramble the Sentence: With Clues" — the whole premise is that the capital letter marks where the sentence begins, but in lane 3 the capitalised tile is the pronoun "I", which is capitalised in every position in English. On that lane the clue is degenerate and teaches a false rule. Exclude "I" from being the capitalised tile.

G1-283 "Unscramble the Sentence: No Clues" — "Find the one order that works" is not true. Lane 4 ("giraffe / is / your / this") admits BOTH "Is this your giraffe?" and "This is your giraffe." The uniqueness claim should be dropped; it is weaker still in free-word-order languages (see the Finnish note below, where I had to change the shipped fi instruction for exactly this reason).

G2-292 "Shopping Math: Buying Three Things" — in the sweep render cards 2 and 3 pose the SAME problem in two wordings (mango + kiwi + strawberry, total 50 c). This is the known raw-draw-order duplicate; please confirm the fix actually reached this face, because the render still shows it.

G2-312 "How Many Days Later?" — only ONE of the four questions on the page asks how many days later; the other three ask a sticker date, a date one week on, and a weekday. Same class as the already-fixed "Dot-to-Dot 1 to 20" title over a 1-10 page.
G2-297 "Read the Calendar: A Busy Month" — the d2 question set is six questions and the page OVERFLOWS: the sweep render is cut off inside question 5 and question 6 is off the sheet entirely.

K-303 "One and Many: Longer Words" — the four-card long-word layout overflows. The fourth card runs to the bottom edge and the "Made with LessonCraftStudio.com" footer, present on every sibling render at the same page size, is missing.

G1-293 "Naming Words and Doing Words" — the heading and instruction use the child register ("naming word" / "doing word") while the bins printed on the same page use the formal class names ("Nouns" / "Verbs"; fi "Substantiivit" / "Verbit"). One page teaches two vocabularies for the same thing. Pick one register, or print both on the bin.

G2-313 "Number Walls with Two-Digit Answers" — "The bricks climb past twenty" understates the page badly: with a four-brick given base of 5-12 the top brick lands around 60-70. The instruction also has no imperative for the actual task, and "add in writing as you go" is opaque for a seven-year-old.

G1-287 "Doubles to 14" — the split divider inside the picture box is drawn on cards 1 and 5 but not on cards 2, 3, 4 and 6 of the same page, so the "two equal groups" cue is inconsistent; and on card 4 (7 + 7) the answer box is clipped by the card bottom edge.
K-315 "Copy the Capitals" — "Look at the capitals, then write THEM yourself" refers to letters, but the task is copying a whole WORD from the card. A child can read it as copying an alphabet.
K-308 "Dot-to-Dot: Count Back from 10" — the page has a highlighted orange start dot, but unlike every sibling dot-to-dot instruction this one never mentions it.

fi DESIGN-RULING MISMATCH (render overrules the brief): the brief states the Finnish articles family is re-targeted to PARTITIVE vs NOMINATIVE ("yksi omena / kaksi omenaa"). The shipped generator does NOT do that. data/b2/articles.js gives fi mode:"form" with chipsFor => [e.singular, e.plural], and LABELS.fi.singularPlural = {one:"yksi", many:"monta"}, so the Finnish pages are SINGULAR vs PLURAL (omena / omenat) with bins headed "yksi" and "monta". I wrote K-306, K-307 and G1-292 to the code and the render. If partitive really is wanted, articles.js has to change first.

fi grammar note on that same family: the bin head "monta" governs the PARTITIVE SINGULAR in Finnish ("monta omenaa"), while the words filed under it are nominative plurals ("omenat"). As a bare category label it is readable, but "monta" + nominative plural is not a grammatical pair; a Finnish reviewer may prefer the school terms "yksikko"/"monikko" or "yksi"/"monet" for the bin heads.

fi data note: data/b2/sentences.js and data/b2/wp-muldiv-frames.js both carry the Finnish entry "crane": "kurkea" — the partitive of kurki, the BIRD — while the artwork at vehicles/crane is a construction crane. lib/b2-common.js B2_EXCLUDE does list fi for crane, so it should never surface; please confirm those two frame tables go through the same exclusion path.

VERIFIED NOT defects for fi (checked against source rather than assumed): the calendar week starts on MONDAY for fi (CALENDAR.fi.weekStart = 1) — the Sunday-first sweep render is an EN artifact only; money renders "snt", not the US cent sign; and the alphabet strip for fi carries a-z plus a-ring, a-umlaut and o-umlaut (COLLATION.fi.strip), so ABC-order pages are correct.
